question: feed image PCs directly as Kalman channels instead of computing a lag -- was this tried?
what_had_been_tried: PCs had been tested against GBTM regions (cumulative dim 1-8 and single PC1-8, all no change) and as a 5-variable block in the cross-sectional factor panel (image_pc_block.json). PCs had NEVER been fed to the Kalman as measurement channels -- that is what this run does.

decisive_structural_finding.reading: 98.5% of fetuses have exactly ONE image study-date. Grouping images by (fetus, study_date) and aligning to true GA gives 922 visits across 908 fetuses. So PCs CANNOT form an image trajectory either -- IMPACT imaging is single-session. This is the same wall the lag hit, confirmed on a different construction, and it is a property of the acquisition protocol.

loadings_on_size_state.reading: PC5 loads +0.132 raw and +0.117 after BMI residualisation -- essentially identical to the lag. PC1, which is 64% of image variance, loads +0.008: the dominant appearance axis is unrelated to fetal size. PC3 drops 0.084 -> 0.080 under BMI adjustment, less than the cross-sectional analysis suggested.

kalman_result.reading: PCs narrow the size-state posterior by 0.28% raw and 0.23% BMI-residualised, against the lag's 0.03%. That is a 9x improvement over the lag -- five channels each carrying a little beats one channel carrying the same -- but 0.28% is still negligible against a state that four biometry measurements already pin down.

ANSWER: Feeding PCs directly is BETTER than computing a lag -- about 9x more narrowing, and it avoids the lag's whole reliability problem since a per-visit PC mean over ~22 images is far better measured than a slot-level lag. But the improvement is 0.28% against 0.03%: both negligible. And the run establishes something more useful than either number -- 98.5% of fetuses have one image session, so no image representation whatsoever can be longitudinal in this cohort.
caveats: PC loadings were estimated by correlating per-fetus PC means with the independent-placement size estimate, then fixed -- not jointly estimated with the state
channel noise set to 1-r^2 assuming standardised channels; a jointly-fitted Psi could differ
the 14 fetuses with 2 image-visits are too few to test whether PCs move within a pregnancy
PCA fitted on all 20,413 IMPACT images at once, so components are cohort-level, not per-visit
